@khalidsaidi/fallback-chain-js — LLM-friendly reference

API:
- fallback(candidates, options?) -> Promise<T>
- createFallbackChain(candidates, options?) -> { run(overrides?), health(), reset() }
- fallbackStream(candidates, options?) -> AsyncGenerator<T>

Candidates:
- () => T | Promise<T>
- { name?: string, run: (ctx) => T | Promise<T> }

AttemptContext passed to each candidate:
- attempt: number
- signal: AbortSignal
- errors: readonly unknown[] (previous attempt errors)

Options:
- signal?: AbortSignal (aborts the whole chain)
- timeoutMs?: number | (ctx) => number | undefined  (per attempt; negative/NaN/non-number throws TypeError — never silently disabled)
- accept?: (value, { attempt }) => boolean
- retryable?: (error, { attempt }) => boolean
- onAttempt?: ({ attempt, name, outcome, durationMs, value?, error? }) => void

Notes:
- attempt is 0-based everywhere (accept/retryable/onAttempt/candidate ctx): first candidate = attempt 0.
- FallbackError (thrown when all candidates fail): .errors = per-attempt errors in order; .named = [{ name?, error }] aligned with .errors; message includes candidate names when candidates are named, e.g. "All 2 fallback candidates failed (primary: Error: boom; backup: TimeoutError: Timed out after 1000ms)".

Outcomes:
- "success": returned accepted value
- "unacceptable": value resolved but accept() returned false => try next
- "rejected": candidate threw/rejected => try next (unless retryable says stop)
- "timeout": timed out => try next
- "aborted": stop immediately and throw

Examples:
1) Basic:
  await fallback([() => primary(), () => secondary()])

2) HTTP fallback on status:
  await fallback(
    [() => fetch(urlA), () => fetch(urlB)],
    { accept: (r) => r.ok }
  )

3) LLM/provider fallback (generic; normalize each provider to one shape):
  await fallback(
    [() => callModel("primary"), () => callModel("backup")],
    { accept: (txt) => typeof txt === "string" && txt.trim().length > 0 }
  )

createFallbackChain (stateful cooldown/health):
- Extra options over fallback(): cooldownMs (default 30000), failureThreshold (default 1), now (injectable clock).
- run(overrides?) merges per-call options (e.g. a request AbortSignal) over the base options.
- Ordering per run: healthy candidates first (original order), cooling-down candidates deprioritized to the end (never skipped outright).
- Failures that count: rejected / timeout / unacceptable. Caller aborts do NOT count.
- Success resets that candidate's failure memory. health() returns { index, name?, consecutiveFailures, coolingDown, cooldownUntil, lastError? }[].

  const chain = createFallbackChain([primary, backup], { cooldownMs: 30_000 });
  const value = await chain.run();

fallbackStream (streaming fallback):
- Candidate: (ctx) => AsyncIterable<T> | AsyncIterator<T> | Iterable<T> (or { name?, run }).
- Falls back on error/timeout/acceptFirstChunk-veto only BEFORE the first chunk is yielded to the consumer.
- After the first chunk: COMMITTED — errors propagate as-is (mid-stream fallback is unsolvable UX; never spliced).
- timeoutMs is the per-attempt budget to the FIRST chunk only.
- acceptFirstChunk(chunk, { attempt }) vetoes a candidate before committing.
- Abandoned candidates: iterator.return() called best-effort; late chunks are dropped, never leaked to the consumer.
- Consumer break/return()/throw() propagates cleanup to the committed inner iterator.
- Clean zero-chunk completion completes the output stream (not an error).

  for await (const token of fallbackStream([primaryStream, backupStream], { timeoutMs: 3000 })) {
    render(token);
  }
